project.name: opencode
project.description: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent available as a CLI and desktop application, built as a Bun-based TypeScript monorepo.

nodes.name: tui
nodes.summary: Initializes and runs the TUI renderer, setting up the keymap, win32 input guards, and rendering the root App component.

nodes.languageNotes: Multi-job pipeline using matrix builds for 6 platform targets (x86_64/aarch64 Linux, macOS, Windows). Uses Azure Trusted Signing for Windows code signing and Apple API keys for macOS notarization.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow handling the GitHub Release creation step, creating or updating release notes and tagging after a successful publish pipeline.

nodes.name: provider.sql.ts

nodes.name: referral.sql.ts

nodes.name: user.ts

nodes.name: cassette.ts

nodes.name: memory

nodes.name: effect.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the core HTTP record-and-replay Effect layers, orchestrating request snapshotting, response capture, redaction, cassette storage, and replay logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Central orchestration module using Effect.js HttpClient layers; separates recording mode, replay mode, and auto mode based on cassette state.

nodes.name: recordingLayer
nodes.summary: Builds an Effect HttpClient Layer that intercepts requests in record, replay, or auto mode; captures responses for recording and plays back cassette interactions for replay.

nodes.name: cassetteLayer

nodes.name: matching.ts

nodes.name: selectSequential
nodes.summary: Finds the first unplayed cassette interaction that matches an incoming request using the provided matcher function, returning detailed diffs if none match.

nodes.name: requestDiff
nodes.summary: Generates a human-readable diff between two request snapshots covering method, URL, headers, and body for diagnostic error messages.

nodes.name: canonicalSnapshot

nodes.name: recorder.ts

nodes.name: resolveAutoMode

nodes.name: redaction.ts

nodes.name: secretFindings

nodes.name: redactHeaders

nodes.name: compose

nodes.name: native-anthropic-tool-loop.json

nodes.name: native-openai-oauth-tool-loop.json

nodes.name: native-zen-tool-loop.json

nodes.name: utilities.css
nodes.summary: Utility CSS classes for common UI patterns: scrollbar hiding (.no-scrollbar), screen-reader visibility (.sr-only), start-truncation (.truncate-start), and a type scale system (.text-12-regular, .text-12-medium, .text-14-medium, etc.) using design token variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses modern CSS nesting for .no-scrollbar pseudo-element targeting and references design token CSS variables for all typography values.

nodes.name: colors.css
nodes.summary: Auto-generated Tailwind v4 @theme block that maps approximately 280 semantic design token CSS custom properties (backgrounds, surfaces, text, borders, icons, syntax highlighting, markdown, and v2 design layer) to Tailwind color utility classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Tailwind v4 @theme block with CSS custom property references; the --color-*: initial reset clears all default Tailwind colors so only these semantic tokens are available.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: Tailwind CSS entry point that establishes layer ordering, imports Tailwind core, and defines the complete design token theme including spacing scale, breakpoints, container sizes, typography, border radii, shadows, and animations before importing colors and custom utilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind v4 @layer declarations and @import with layer() syntax; the --*: initial reset in @theme clears all Tailwind defaults so only explicitly declared tokens are active.

nodes.name: utilities.css
nodes.summary: Defines custom Tailwind v4 utility classes for the UI package: no-scrollbar (cross-browser scrollbar hiding), badge-mask and badge-mask-tight (CSS mask cutouts for notification badges), truncate-start (RTL text truncation), and fade-up-text (staggered entrance animation with up to 30 sequenced child delays).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind v4 @utility blocks which register atomic utilities; the fade-up-text utility encodes 30 nth-child animation delays inline to avoid JavaScript dependency for staggered animations.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses CSS nesting (nested slot selectors inside the component rule) and data-attribute selectors. Sets global font-smoothing via the universal * selector reset at the top.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses the accessibility pattern of a visually-hidden real input (clip/overflow) paired with a custom styled control. Checked/indeterminate icon visibility is toggled via display:none rather than opacity to avoid layout impact.

nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 modal dialog component including the scrim overlay, centered container (480x368px default), scrollable content area, header with title/description/close button, body, and footer, with large and x-large size variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Hides scrollbars cross-browser (scrollbar-width: none, -ms-overflow-style, ::-webkit-scrollbar). Pointer-events flow: the outer dialog wrapper is pointer-events:none while the inner container is pointer-events:auto.

nodes.summary: Minimal styles for the diff-changes display component showing line addition and deletion counts, with green and red semantic colouring via design-system state tokens.

nodes.name: icon-button-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 icon-only button component with four variants (neutral, contrast, ghost, ghost-muted), three size variants (20/24/28px), layered gradient hover/pressed states, and disabled handling mirroring button-v2.
nodes.languageNotes: The ghost-muted variant uses icon-muted colour token for the idle state and shares the same overlay hover/pressed pattern as the other variants.

nodes.name: inline-input-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 inline input component that pairs a labelled prefix section with a plain text field, supporting hover, focus, invalid, and disabled states, a numeric mode, an optional configurable label width, and an embedded icon button.

nodes.name: keybind-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 keyboard shortcut display component, rendering small 14x14px key badges in neutral (with bg) or ghost (transparent) variants with consistent label typography.

nodes.name: line-comment-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 line comment component in two variants: a display (read) mode showing author avatar, text, and overflow menu, and an editor mode with a textarea, label, footer meta, and action buttons.

nodes.name: menu-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 dropdown menu component, covering the floating content panel with an entrance animation, menu items with content/shortcut/badge/indicator/chevron slots, separator, group label, hover and checked states, and disabled handling.
nodes.languageNotes: The enter animation uses scale(0.96) -> scale(1) with opacity for a subtle pop-in effect. transform-origin is driven by the KobalteJS --kb-menu-content-transform-origin CSS variable.

nodes.name: radio-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 radio group and radio item components, using the same visually-hidden input pattern as checkbox-v2, with circular controls (border-radius: 9999px), checked/hover/invalid/disabled states, and an inner dot indicator.
nodes.languageNotes: Radio control uses a round dot (6x6px) as the selection indicator, positioned absolutely centred inside the 16x16px control circle.

nodes.name: segmented-control-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 segmented control (pill tab group) component, defining a 232px wide row container with equal-flex items that show a pressed/active state via background and inset border.

nodes.name: select-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 select/dropdown component, extending menu-v2.css with slide-down open/close animations on the content panel, a trigger shell aligned to text-input-v2 dimensions, a rotating chevron, a scrollable listbox, and selected-item accent highlighting.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports menu-v2.css directly via @import, reusing all menu item styles and adding select-specific animation keyframes and trigger layout on top.

nodes.name: switch-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 toggle switch component with a 24x16px track, a 12x12px animated thumb that translates 8px on activation, hover width expansion for tactile feel, checked/invalid/disabled/readonly states, and a visually-hidden native input.
nodes.languageNotes: Thumb hover expansion (12->13px width with border-radius change) gives a physical 'squish' micro-interaction without JavaScript.

nodes.name: tabs-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 tabs component with three visual variants (normal underline, pill, settings vertical) and both horizontal and vertical orientations, handling tab list scrolling, close buttons, selected state border/background, and section titles for settings mode.
nodes.languageNotes: The normal horizontal variant uses a ::before pseudo-element on the tab list to draw a full-bleed bottom border, extending 8px beyond the list's padded area using negative left offset and calc.

nodes.name: text-input-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles for the v2 plain text input component with hover, focus, invalid, and disabled states, a numeric mode, an optional inline icon button, and error colour propagation to the caret and placeholder text.

nodes.name: text-shimmer-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles the TextShimmerV2 component, implementing a per-character gradient sweep animation that transitions text from a muted base color to a peak highlight color, with full support for reduced-motion preferences and a `background-clip: text` progressive enhancement.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CSS custom properties for per-character staggered animation delay via `--_index`, and a `@supports` block to apply background-clip text gradient only when supported, with a graceful opacity-based fallback.

nodes.name: textarea-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles the TextareaV2 form component, covering layout, hover, focus, invalid, and disabled states with smooth transitions for background, outline, and shadow using design-token CSS variables.

nodes.name: toast-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles the ToastV2 notification system including the fixed-position region container, individual toast cards with pop-in/pop-out keyframe animations, and all interior slots (header, icon, title, description, actions, close button).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CSS nesting (native, no preprocessor) to scope slot selectors inside the region and toast component selectors, keeping specificity consistent.

nodes.name: tool-error-card-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles the ToolErrorCardV2 component, a collapsible error display card with a danger-colored left border, animated loading spinner, chevron rotation on expand, and typography slots for title, subtitle, separator, and suffix.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines a suite of semantic CSS custom properties (--tec-*) scoped to the component root to centralize color theming, making it easy to override without touching individual slot rules.

nodes.name: tooltip-v2.css
nodes.summary: Styles the TooltipV2 floating overlay, defining compact typography, floating shadow, border-radius, and scale-based open/close keyframe animations anchored to a transform-origin CSS variable supplied by the positioning library.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `--kb-tooltip-content-transform-origin` (set by the Kobalte tooltip primitive) to animate scale from the correct anchor point.

nodes.name: colors.css
nodes.summary: Defines the complete v2 design system raw color palette as CSS custom properties within a @layer theme block, covering grey scales, alpha dark/light transparency steps, and 8 hue ramps (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink) each with 12 stop gradations from 100 to 1200.
nodes.languageNotes: All variables follow the `--v2-<hue>-<stop>` naming convention inside a CSS `@layer theme`, ensuring predictable cascade priority when consumed by theme.css.

nodes.name: tailwind.css
nodes.summary: Entry-point stylesheet that composes the v2 design system by importing the raw color palette (colors.css) and the semantic theme token layer (theme.css) in a single file.

nodes.name: theme.css
nodes.summary: Maps raw color palette tokens to semantic design-system roles (background, text, icon, border, overlay, state, elevation, illustration, and font) and provides both explicit light (`[data-color-scheme='light']`) and dark (`[data-color-scheme='dark']`) variants controlled via a data attribute on the root element.
nodes.languageNotes: A commented-out `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block is present but disabled; theming is instead driven by the `data-color-scheme` attribute, allowing runtime JS or Storybook to toggle themes without relying on OS preferences.

layers.name: CLI Agent
layers.description: The main opencode CLI, TUI interface, HTTP API server, and agent orchestration — the primary runnable product that handles sessions, tools, providers, and real-time event streaming via Effect-TS.

layers.name: Core Domain & LLM
layers.description: Cross-package domain services (account, agent catalog, AI SDK adapters) and the LLM client library implementing multi-provider protocol adapters, prompt caching, and tool invocation against Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Bedrock.

layers.name: Console Product
layers.description: The cloud-hosted management console (SolidStart + SST on Cloudflare/PlanetScale) providing workspace management, session browsing, authentication, and billing for teams using opencode.

layers.name: Web & Public Sites
layers.description: The Astro/Starlight documentation site and public web presence for opencode, including the session-share viewer component and the Mintlify-based API documentation.

layers.name: Desktop Application
layers.description: The Electron-based desktop app and the SolidJS frontend app package it hosts, providing the primary GUI for interacting with opencode sessions, timelines, and settings outside the terminal.

layers.name: UI Component Library
layers.description: The shared SolidJS design-system component library used by the desktop app and console, along with Storybook stories for component development and visual testing.

layers.name: Integrations & SDKs
layers.description: External-facing integration surfaces: the JavaScript and Python SDKs, the VS Code extension, Slack integration, Cloudflare Worker share function, enterprise sharing, data-lake stats pipeline, and supporting utilities like the HTTP cassette recorder and Effect-Drizzle-SQLite adapter.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Deployment
layers.description: SST v3 infrastructure definitions, container Dockerfiles, GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, Nix flakes, release and utility scripts, and deployment patches that provision and operate all opencode services across AWS, Cloudflare, and self-hosted environments.

layers.name: Project Configuration & Documentation
layers.description: Monorepo-level configuration (package.json, tsconfig, turbo, oxlint, Prettier), project documentation (multilingual READMEs, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, AGENTS.md), AI agent context files in .opencode/, API specs in specs/, and developer tooling config (.husky, .zed, architecture artifacts).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what opencode is: an open-source AI coding agent built as a Bun-based TypeScript monorepo. It covers installation, the desktop app, web console, CLI usage, and provider configuration — giving you the vocabulary and mental model you need before diving into code. Reading this first ensures that terms like 'provider', 'session', 'TUI', and 'MCP' mean something concrete when you encounter them in the source.

tour.title: CLI Entry & Bootstrap
tour.description: The CLI binary shim at `bin/opencode` is the real starting point for users: it detects the host platform and architecture, locates the correct compiled binary, and hands off execution. The CONTRIBUTING guide explains how to run each layer of the monorepo locally (API server, web app, desktop, debugger), making it essential reading before you trace anything deeper into the stack.
tour.languageLesson: Bun and Node.js can share the same launcher shim: the shim uses dynamic 'require' or import to pick the right pre-compiled binary at runtime, so the published npm package contains platform-specific binaries and a single JS entry that selects among them.

tour.title: Effect-TS Runtime Foundation
tour.description: The entire backend is built on Effect-TS, a typed functional-programming runtime for TypeScript. `app-runtime.ts` assembles the full `AppLayer` by composing every major service — it is the composition root of the application. `instance-state.ts` provides a per-directory `ScopedCache` that isolates state for multi-project and multi-worktree usage. `bus/index.ts` is a typed pub/sub message bus (fan-in: 63 files depend on it) that bridges synchronous Effect code with the event-driven TUI and HTTP server.
tour.languageLesson: Effect-TS services are declared with a 'Tag' and provided via 'Layer'. The AppLayer composes all service layers using 'Layer.mergeAll' and 'Layer.provide', producing a dependency-injection container that is type-checked at compile time. Layers model resource acquisition and release, ensuring cleanup on shutdown.

tour.title: Configuration & Core Schemas
tour.description: `config/config.ts` (fan-in: 71) loads and merges opencode configuration from global and project-level files, resolving provider settings, model choices, keybinds, and experimental flags. `session/schema.ts` (fan-in: 81) is the highest fan-in file in the project — it defines `SessionID`, `MessageID`, and `PartID` as Effect Schema branded types that flow through every layer. Understanding these two files gives you the shared vocabulary of the entire codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Effect Schema branded types (e.g. 'SessionID' derived from a string) give nominal identity to primitive values at the type level, preventing accidental mixing of IDs from different domains while keeping the runtime representation as a plain string. Schema.decode validates and transforms at the boundary where external data enters the system.

tour.title: Agent Core & Session Management
tour.description: `agent/agent.ts` (fan-in: 52) is the Effect service that embodies the agent loop — it provides agent info types and the default implementation. `session/session.ts` (fan-in: 51) handles CRUD, message persistence, forking, archiving, and permission management for sessions. Together, these two files represent the heart of what opencode does: a structured conversation with an AI that can read and modify your codebase. The AGENTS.md document explains the coding conventions AI agents and contributors should follow when working inside this codebase.

tour.title: Prompt Engine & AI Loop
tour.description: `session/prompt.ts` is the main prompt execution engine — it orchestrates the full AI coding agent loop including tool calls, compaction, instruction building, and streaming. This is where a user's message is transformed into an LLM request, tool calls are dispatched, results are fed back, and the loop continues until a final answer is produced. Understanding this file reveals how all the surrounding services plug together during an actual coding session.
tour.languageLesson: The agent loop in opencode uses Effect's fiber-based concurrency: each turn of the loop is an Effect that can be interrupted, retried, or forked. Effect's 'Stream' type enables streaming LLM tokens back to the caller while the loop continues processing tool calls asynchronously.

tour.title: Tools & Permissions
tour.description: `tool/registry.ts` is the central tool registry that assembles all built-in and plugin-provided tools, normalizes their JSON schemas, and exposes the combined set to the agent. Tools represent the agent's capabilities: reading files, writing code, running shell commands, and more. `permission/index.ts` guards those capabilities: it manages interactive approval flows, persistent allow/deny rules, and per-session permission policies — ensuring users remain in control of what the agent can do.

tour.title: AI Providers & MCP
tour.description: `provider/provider.ts` is the central AI provider service managing discovery, initialization, and SDK resolution for all supported providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Google, and many others). `mcp/index.ts` manages Model Context Protocol server connections — the emerging standard for giving agents access to external tools and context. `plugin/index.ts` ties both together by loading plugins that can register custom auth, model, and tool hooks from configuration.
tour.languageLesson: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that defines a JSON-RPC interface between AI agents and external services. opencode implements an MCP client in Effect-TS, allowing any MCP-compatible server to expose tools and resources that the agent can call alongside its built-in tools.

tour.title: HTTP API Server
tour.description: `server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts` is the Hono-based HTTP API server that exposes the entire agent capability surface over HTTP — session management, provider configuration, file operations, sync, and more. This is the integration point between the core logic (Steps 3–8) and every client: the TUI, desktop app, web console, and external SDKs all communicate through this server. `server/server.ts` handles the lower-level concerns: port binding with fallback, mDNS advertisement for local discovery, and graceful shutdown.
tour.languageLesson: Hono is a lightweight TypeScript HTTP framework that runs on Bun, Deno, Node.js, and edge runtimes. opencode uses Hono's typed router with Zod/Effect Schema validation, so every API route has compile-time type safety from the request schema to the response type.

tour.title: Terminal UI (TUI)
tour.description: `cli/cmd/tui/app.tsx` is the root SolidJS component that bootstraps the terminal UI, setting up all context providers, the keymap, command palette, routing, and plugin initialization. Built with ink (React/Solid for terminals), it renders the full interactive coding experience in your terminal. `cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx` is the primary session route — it orchestrates message rendering, keyboard handling, and the streaming agent response display that users interact with during a coding session.
tour.languageLesson: opencode's TUI is built with SolidJS rather than React, using SolidJS's fine-grained reactivity to update only the specific DOM nodes that change. In a terminal context this means only re-rendering the cells that actually changed, which dramatically reduces flickering and improves performance for fast-streaming AI output.

tour.title: JavaScript SDK
tour.description: `packages/sdk/js/src/index.ts` is the public entry point of the official JavaScript/TypeScript SDK that external projects use to connect to opencode. `client.ts` wraps the generated HTTP client with opencode-specific request rewriting and auth injection. The SDK provides a clean, versioned API contract that hides the HTTP details — it is how integrations like the Slack bot, GitHub Actions, and third-party tools communicate with the opencode server.

tour.title: Desktop App (Electron)
tour.description: `packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts` is the Electron main process entry point. It bootstraps the app lifecycle including proxy configuration, sidecar server management (spawning the opencode HTTP server as a child process), and native window management. The desktop app is a thin Electron shell that embeds the web-based UI and manages the lifecycle of the opencode backend, demonstrating how the HTTP API from Step 9 enables multiple client surfaces.
tour.languageLesson: Electron apps split into a 'main' process (Node.js, full OS access) and 'renderer' processes (Chromium, sandboxed). The main process in opencode spawns the opencode HTTP server as a sidecar child process and communicates with the renderer via IPC, keeping the AI workload out of the renderer's main thread.

tour.title: Cloud Infrastructure (SST/AWS/Cloudflare)
tour.description: `sst.config.ts` defines the entire cloud infrastructure using SST v3: it conditionally loads modules for the web app, data lake, stats service, console, enterprise tier, and monitoring depending on the deployment stage. SST v3 deploys to both AWS (Lambda, RDS, S3) and Cloudflare Workers, giving opencode its hosted console at opencode.ai alongside the self-hosted CLI model.
tour.languageLesson: SST v3 uses a TypeScript-first infrastructure-as-code model where cloud resources are declared as typed objects. Unlike Terraform, SST generates IAM permissions automatically from resource references, and live development mode (sst dev) proxies Lambda invocations to local code without redeployment.

tour.title: Containerization
tour.description: The opencode CLI Dockerfile uses a multi-architecture build strategy to produce a minimal Alpine-based image with separate build stages for amd64 and arm64. The builder stage installs Bun, TypeScript dependencies, and compiles the binary; the runtime stage copies only the compiled output into a scratch-based image. The `packages/containers/` directory contains additional specialized images used in CI/CD for building the Rust components, Tauri desktop app, and publishing artifacts.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-architecture Docker builds use the 'TARGETARCH' build argument to select platform-specific stages. In monorepos, Docker BuildKit's cache mounts (--mount=type=cache) dramatically speed up builds by persisting package manager caches across CI runs without baking them into the final image layers.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: The `test.yml` workflow runs the full test suite (Bun unit tests via Turbo and Playwright e2e tests) on every push, forming the quality gate for the codebase. The `publish.yml` pipeline is the release pipeline that builds and distributes opencode across all platforms — npm, GitHub Releases, Homebrew, and container registries — triggered when a version tag is pushed. Together these workflows close the loop from code change to shipped artifact.
tour.languageLesson: Turborepo (turbo.json) enables task-level caching and parallelism across the monorepo: it tracks input hashes for each package's build/test tasks and skips re-execution when inputs haven't changed. This makes CI proportionally fast even as the monorepo grows, since only affected packages re-run their pipelines.
